title: The Deposit Slip That Didn't Match
script:
On a Tuesday morning, Dolores walked into her bank and was told her account had been closed nine months earlier. She had been depositing into it every single Friday.

The teller checked the receipts in Dolores's blue envelope. Dolores had given the money to Harold at the church office, and Harold had given her a receipt each time.

Harold had been the church treasurer for nine years. When the church changed banks, he brought new green slips and said the numbering system had changed.

The account on those slips belonged to a holding company Harold had registered after his wife died. It had no office and no employees. Its only regular activity was receiving church deposits and sending money back when someone asked for a withdrawal.

The blue envelope held receipts for forty one thousand, eight hundred and sixteen dollars. The bank account held nothing.
